hook: One ancient clay tablet recorded a royal tragedy buried for 3,400 years.

sections.voiceover: One ancient clay tablet recorded a royal tragedy buried for 3,400 years.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up cinematic shot of cuneiform script carved into an ancient clay tablet under dim museum lighting.
sections.sfx_cue: Subtle low frequency drone with a faint scraping texture.
b_roll: Kayalıpınar archaeological site wide aerial shot
sections.animation_cue: Slow zoom in on the carved wedge-shaped characters.

sections.voiceover: Archaeologists working at Kayalıpınar in central Turkey discovered 131 cuneiform tablets. Turkey's Minister of Culture and Tourism Mehmet Nuri Ersoy announced the find. What secrets did King Tudhaliya II hide in the royal archive?
sections.visual_cue: Medium shot of archaeologists carefully brushing soil off a discovered artifact in a dusty trench at Kayalıpınar.
b_roll: Mehmet Nuri Ersoy speaking at a press conference
sections.animation_cue: Pan across the uncovered tablet surface.

sections.voiceover: Combining the 131 tablets with 53 pieces found in 2025 at Šamuḥa makes 184 total archive pieces.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up tracking shot of multiple cataloged clay fragments resting on padded museum shelves.
sections.sfx_cue: Subtle paper shuffle and soft room tone.

sections.voiceover: The 131 newly found tablets reveal a brutal epidemic during the reign of King Tudhaliya II. These 131 cuneiform tablets from Turkey detail a deadly epidemic that killed a nursing princess.
sections.visual_cue: Macro close-up shot of damaged clay edges revealing detailed cuneiform markings under raking light.
sections.animation_cue: Highlight overlay pulsing over specific cuneiform lines.

sections.voiceover: 131 cuneiform tablets revealed a lost royal tragedy.
sections.visual_cue: Static wide shot of the excavated Kayalıpınar site at dusk with shadows stretching across the trench.
